title: Catalog API Pagination Contract Handoff Plan
purpose: Proposed handoff assembled from source-linked outcomes; human source review and approval required.

scope.text: GET /v1/items returns a JSON object with an items array and next_cursor string.
UI must support moving to the next page.
GET /v1/items returns a top-level JSON array and uses page and page_size query parameters.

requirements.text: GET /v1/items returns a JSON object with an items array and next_cursor string.
UI must support moving to the next page.
GET /v1/items returns a top-level JSON array and uses page and page_size query parameters.

stories.text: Only if an authorized human selects alternative BEH-api-a-response-shape in unresolved decision DEC-catalog-api-pagination: GET /v1/items returns a JSON object with an items array and next_cursor string.
acceptance_criteria: Only if an authorized human selects alternative BEH-api-a-response-shape in unresolved decision DEC-catalog-api-pagination: When GET /v1/items is called under Draft A, the HTTP response body is a single JSON object, not a top-level array.
Only if an authorized human selects alternative BEH-api-a-response-shape in unresolved decision DEC-catalog-api-pagination: The JSON object contains an items array field.

Only if an authorized human selects alternative BEH-api-a-response-shape in unresolved decision DEC-catalog-api-pagination: The JSON object contains a next_cursor string field whose value may be used to request a subsequent page.
Only if an authorized human selects alternative BEH-api-a-response-shape in unresolved decision DEC-catalog-api-pagination: Draft A does not define page or page_size query parameters for pagination.

stories.text: UI must support moving to the next page.
acceptance_criteria: Under the Draft A contract, the UI exposes an observable next-page action that transitions the user to the next set of items using the supplied next_cursor value.

stories.text: Only if an authorized human selects alternative BEH-api-b-response-shape in unresolved decision DEC-catalog-api-pagination: GET /v1/items returns a top-level JSON array and uses page and page_size query parameters.
acceptance_criteria: Only if an authorized human selects alternative BEH-api-b-response-shape in unresolved decision DEC-catalog-api-pagination: When GET /v1/items is called under Draft B, the HTTP response body is a top-level JSON array, not an object with an items field.

Only if an authorized human selects alternative BEH-api-b-response-shape in unresolved decision DEC-catalog-api-pagination: Pagination is requested using page and page_size query parameters; the response does not include a next_cursor string.

open_questions: Which GET /v1/items pagination contract should apply: Draft A, which returns a JSON object with an items array and next_cursor string, or Draft B, which returns a top-level JSON array using page and page_size query parameters?
Who has authority to select the authoritative Catalog API contract, given api-spec-b states 'Neither draft is approved; the authoritative contract has not been selected'?

For the Draft A contract, how does a client supply the next_cursor value on a subsequent GET /v1/items request (for example, query parameter, header, or request body), and what request format is used for the first page when no cursor exists?
For the Draft A contract, what is the exact meaning of an empty, null, or absent next_cursor, and what response or error semantics indicate that no further pages are available?

Does BEH-api-a-ui-next-page apply only when the Draft A cursor contract is selected? If Draft B is selected, what UI pagination behavior is expected, given api-spec-b does not define a UI next-page requirement?
For the Draft B contract, how are page and page_size query parameters supplied, including their names, whether they are required or optional, and any default or maximum values?
For the Draft B contract, how should the client interpret an empty top-level JSON array or an out-of-range page value, and what exhaustion or error semantics must be handled?

Which user/UI behavior should apply under Draft B's page/page_size contract, given the source specifies only the API and not a UI pagination behavior? Is BEH-api-a-ui-next-page also required under Draft B, or is a different UI required?
Who owns or approves the Catalog API pagination contract and the UI pagination behavior delivery?
What is the delivery date or milestone for the selected Catalog API pagination contract and UI pagination behavior?
